newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers union reached a tentative labor contract.
* Ohio Edison Co and Centerior Energy Corp said they agreed to merge in a stock swap valued at $1.61 billion.
* Intuit Inc agreed to sell its electronic bill payment processing unit to CheckFree Corp for $227 million in stock.
* International Business Machines Corp is planning to offer buyouts or other inducements to 3,000 to 5,000 employees.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose 50.68 points to close at 5889.20, another record.
* Crestar Financial Corp agreed to buy Citizens Bancorp for about $774 million.
* Goldman Sachs posted a pretax profit of $589 million in its third quarter, a 39-percent rise.
* Archer Daniels Midland Co said two former executives would step down from its board.
* Foundation Health Corp said it was discussing a possible merger.
* America Online Inc moved its stock listing to the New York Stock Exchange from the Nasdaq National Market.

* The former chairman of the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), Zoltan Guttman, was fined $500,000 by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission and barred from commodities trading for five years for his part in an alleged fictitious trading scheme.
